title: COMMISSION STAFF WORKING DOCUMENT EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF THE EVALUATION of the 2019-2024 Protocol to the Agreement on a Sustainable Fisheries Partnership between the European Union and the Republic of Senegal
text:
EN
EN
EUROPEAN
COMMISSION
Brussels, 13.1.2026
SWD(2026) 6 final
COMMISSION STAFF WORKING DOCUMENT
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF THE EVALUATION
of the 2019-2024 Protocol to the Agreement on a Sustainable Fisheries Partnership
between the European Union and the Republic of Senegal
{SWD(2026) 5 final}
1
Under the external dimension of the EU’s common fisheries policy (CFP)1, the Commission is
responsible for the negotiation of implementing protocols to sustainable fisheries partnership
agreements (SFPAs) with non-EU countries, and for the implementation of those protocols.
SFPAs create a legal, environmental, economic and social governance framework for fishing
activities carried out by EU fishing vessels in non-EU waters. In return, the EU pays financial
compensation to the partner country for access to its waters and provides it with financial
support for the implementation of a national strategy on fisheries and the blue economy. The
EU contribution is supplemented by fees payable by EU vessel owners.
Before submitting a recommendation to the Council asking it to authorise the opening of
negotiations for a successor protocol to a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement, the
Commission arranges for independent ex ante and ex post evaluations of each protocol, in
accordance with Article 31(10) of the CFP Basic Regulation1.
This staff working document (SWD) contains an ex post evaluation of the application of the
most recent implementing protocol (‘the implementing protocol’) to the sustainable fisheries
partnership agreement between the European Union and the Republic of Senegal (‘the
Agreement’). These evaluations are based mainly on an independent evaluation carried out by
an external consultant2. The external consultant undertook extensive consultations with
stakeholders in the EU and in Senegal. During the evaluation process, the consultant engaged
in discussions with the European and Senegalese authorities to gather their views on the
implementation of the 2019-2024 protocol.
The ex post evaluation covers the period up to March 2024, which is most of the period of
application of the 2019-2024 implementing protocol. It provides an overall assessment of the
implementing protocol, drawing conclusions on its effectiveness, efficiency, relevance,
coherence and acceptance and on the EU added value of the intervention. The detailed issues
raised by these evaluation criteria are set out in further detail in Section 4 of the evaluation
report.
The external contractor’s final report also presents an ex ante study evaluating the future of the
sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the EU and Senegal. However, in keeping
with the EU’s zero tolerance policy on illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, and
considering the Commission’s decision to pre-identify Senegal as a non-cooperating country in
the fight against IUU fishing3, the Commission does not intend to recommend opening
negotiations for a successor protocol. The Commission therefore does not, at this point, need to
conduct and present its ex ante evaluation in this Commission staff working document.
This evaluation covers only the implementation of the 2019-2024 protocol to the sustainable
fisheries partnership agreement between the European Union and Senegal. It is independent of
the aforementioned Commission decision to pre-identify Senegal as a non-cooperating country
in the fight against IUU fishing and cannot pre-empt potential developments in connection with
that decision in the context of the application of the IUU Regulation.
1Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2013 on the Common
Fisheries Policy (OJ L 354, 28.12.2013, p. 22).
2 Évaluation rétrospective et prospective du protocole à l’accord de partenariat dans le domaine de la pêche durable entre
l’Union Européenne et la République du Sénégal – Rapport final, Publications Office of the European Union, 2024,
https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2771/806730.
3 Commission Decision of 27 May 2024 as regards the notification to the Republic of Senegal of the possibility of being
identified as a non-cooperating third country in fighting illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, C/2024/3319, OJ C,
C/2024/3277, 29.5.2024.
